extracted.intended_audience: Graduate students applying to the U.S. DOE Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing and submitting a SCGSR program application, including required application fields, proposal content, supporting documents, letters of support, and submission rules/timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use online application system; materials are sole basis for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications to the SCGSR program must be completed through the online application system. Materials uploaded into the online application system will provide the sole basis for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the application deadline and become familiar with the application information requested. The online application system will guide applicants through the application requirements. Only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for evaluation and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete all required fields in the online application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete all required fields in the online application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields include: Contact Information; Academic Information, including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information, such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCGSR Research Proposal content and development
rubrics_metrics.description: The SCGSR research proposal is developed by the applying graduate student in collaboration with a collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist, and in consultation with the student’s primary graduate thesis advisor. It includes the scope of thesis research proposed to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research proposal must be submitted online with the online application. Guidelines for development of the research proposal, as well as specific proposal format and required elements, are provided via the program's proposal guidelines link. Applicants are recommended to review the Application Evaluation and Selection guidance prior to completing the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate application prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicate Application: An application whose SCGSR research proposal is the same as that of a SCGSR application already awarded from a previous SCGSR solicitation cycle is a duplicate application and will NOT be considered in any other SCGSR solicitation cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit a proposal that duplicates a previously awarded SCGSR proposal; such submissions will be excluded from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload official graduate transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to upload a PDF copy of their current graduate transcripts to the online application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcript must be current and official. Submitted official transcripts must have all Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth redacted or removed prior to uploading. Any applications found to contain PII in the form of Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth will be deemed non-compliant and will not be considered. View details on submitting acceptable transcripts via the provided link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide proof of Ph.D. candidacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide official proof that they have successfully completed the Ph.D. candidacy requirements at their current graduate institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submitted official transcript does not explicitly show the applicant’s Ph.D. candidacy status (i.e., the words “Ph.D. candidacy” or “Ph.D. candidate” and the date/term), the applicant is required to submit additional official proof. Acceptable additional official forms of proof for Ph.D. candidacy are: (1) an official, signed letter from the applicant’s university/college Registrar’s office; or (2) an official, signed letter from the Chair of the applicant’s academic department. The letter must describe: (a) the institution’s/department’s/program’s requirements for Ph.D. candidacy (including the URL, if available online), (b) how the applicant fulfills the requirements, and (c) the date or academic term when the applicant achieved his or her Ph.D. candidacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two required Letters of Support and their sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Two Letters of Support are required: one from the graduate student’s primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants request the Letters of Support through the online application system by providing contact information; the system sends automated email notifications with instructions. These individuals must submit their letter of support through the online portal using the instructions provided. Letters of Support are due before the application closing date and cannot be submitted outside the online application system. Applicants are encouraged to begin discussions about the proposed research early so letters can be completed with full knowledge of the proposed research and the applicant’s preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support submission process and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters must be submitted through the online application portal using the system's instructions and are due before the application closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide accurate contact information in the system to trigger automated email instructions to letter writers. Letters cannot be submitted outside the online system. Begin outreach to letter writers early to ensure timely submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Identifiable Information (PII) handling for transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted official transcripts must have all Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth redacted or removed prior to uploading into the application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are considered protected PII and must not be shared. Any applications found to contain PII in the form of Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth will be deemed non-compliant and will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to review Application Evaluation and Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that the applicant review the Application Evaluation and Selection prior to completing the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing the evaluation/selection criteria will help applicants prepare materials that align with how submissions are assessed (link provided on the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available resources (video guides and previous workshops)
rubrics_metrics.description: Video Guides and Previous Workshops are available to assist applicants with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickable video guides are provided for transcripts and proof of PhD candidacy, letters of support, priority research areas and merit review criteria, and other topics; applicants should use these resources to understand requirements and improve submissions.
